spec: Owner's design review of theorem.rs, 2026-11-16: reading surface, composer, sidebar, top chrome, settings, Kit and Theo
rules: built is the implementer's report; review is set only by the owner. Nothing is accepted until the owner says so.
Subjective changes get a visual target the owner picks (study or fixture with Theorem's own components) before code spreads.
Evidence names the state it shows; an empty page or an error reply does not evidence a normal reply.
rejected_decisions: No visible quiet band over the Life field (was READ-01)
The composer is not an opaque cutout; it keeps its liquid glass (was READ-07, COMP-05 opacity)
Settings keeps its original linear layout; only its information architecture changes (was SET-01)

items.claim: Life glyphs go quiet under each line of response text, following the lines (no rectangular band), and the field keeps running between lines and in the margins; turning Life off changes only the background
items.note: lib/life/occlusion.ts (per-cell coverage from Range.getClientRects, feathered) applied in mount-life.ts and mount-life-2d.ts from life-backdrop.tsx. 2026-11-17 review (Life still competes with paragraphs): the WebGL mask snapped each line to whole cells through projectClientToGrid, which also returned -Infinity for a line crossing the grid edge, so part of a paragraph went unmasked; it now projects fractional cells from the canvas and grid metrics. Each line rect is extended to the block line-height, so no strip of field shows between lines, and reaches 14px past its ends; coverage from neighbouring lines sums; TEXT_QUIET is 0.97. 3x crops in both themes show paragraphs clean, with the field running in the margins. Typing benchmark, 75 keystrokes over 2.9s, three runs each (CDP Performance): script 1305ms with Life on vs 914ms off, of which the idle field loop is 662 vs 337ms, so typing itself costs about 66ms more with Life on (under 1ms a key) and layout is unchanged (19.6 vs 19.3ms). 2026-11-17 (10:24 review) recheck: populated-shell, Expressive stone, field on, 3x in both themes after the gradient change: no glyph on any line, no opaque band; no further change made. One animation frame per theme was checked.

items.claim: The + menu's Skills submenu is a skills browser: Plan, then the skills Theorem serves from its registry with their plugin, and a link to browse skills in settings; picking one writes a skill chip into the draft that the turn's model loads
items.built: UI done; live skill load blocked in Theorem
items.note: composer-plus.tsx over lib/theorem/catalog (/api/chat/v1/skills). A pick writes assistant-ui's directive :skill[title]{name=id}; user-markdown.tsx renders it as a chip by title. Live gate (scripts/e2e/skills.mjs, bun run e2e:skills, local stack, 2026-11-17): the submenu lists the 8 skills Theorem serves, the pick writes the directive, focus returns to the draft. The first run found the composer's Markdown export escaping the bracket (:skill\[...]), so the sent message showed no chip and the model got escaped text; composer-markdown.ts now keeps skill directives as it keeps tool directives (test in composer-markdown.test.tsx). After the fix the sent message carries the directive intact and shows the chip. The turn itself fails in Theorem: the chat front has no skill_get (it is on the MCP surface in crates/api, not in crates/agent), tool() is ungranted inside execute_program, and search_tools and describe return without a disposition so program_turn.rs result_disposition marks them failed; the model searched for SKILL.md files and hit the 24-iteration limit. The integration gate stays open on that Theorem work.

items.claim: Every + menu row's icon is from one family with the composer's attach and + controls

items.claim: The liquid composer's edge is lit from the top and fades down, with a contact shadow under it, staying glass
items.note: The live pane's flat focus ring drew the bottom edge as bright as the top; it is gone, and the pane's own contour is the edge (dark --lg-stroke 0.16 on the composer). Measured at 3x in dark: top edge 99 as before, bottom edge 46 to 26 (the body's value), a darker contact below from --liquid-contact. Focus shows as the caret; forced colors still draws the border. 2026-11-17 review (light rim too bright at the top and corners): the light composer takes --lg-stroke 0.22, --lg-light 0.16, --lg-sheen 0.05. Measured at 3x in light: the top hairline 254 to 247, the glow 2px in 233 to 207, 7px in 212 to 197; the refraction and blur are unchanged.

items.claim: The navigation panel and the rail's attached corners use a 15px radius, matching messages, code blocks, artifacts and the composer
items.note: shell/floating-card.tsx FLOATING_CARD_VARS --panel-radius 15px (was 14px); styles.css .rail-junction --junction-corner 15px (was 10px). The owner asked for the sidebar curves at 15px; the design review had flagged --junction-corner for a separate look, so it is called out here.

items.claim: Under glass, the navigation panel is the composer's glass, and the rail's tab, concave corners included, is drawn by the same liquid-glass renderer in the same material, lit across the panel's box, so composer, panel and tab read as one material
items.note: styles.css --composer-glass-* tokens applied to [data-surface-role=composer|navigation].surface-liquid; floating-card.tsx uses surface-liquid instead of glass-panel/glass-panel-liquid (that utility is now used only by stories/glass-compare.tsx). The panel keeps its own panel-lift shadow and clearer lower third. appearance.css junction veil = composer tone at --lg-body*(1-show) over --sheet-field. Measured at 3x and 1x: tab vs panel body within 1-2 levels in both themes, before and after the gradient change. 2026-11-17 follow-up (owner: the tab did not look like the same component): the tab was CSS only (a flat veil). rail.tsx Junction now runs useLiquidGlass on the tab (curved on the rail side, running on into the panel), with the composer-glass tokens and the sheet's field under it instead of a blur of the rail; the renderer takes a light box (Pane.light, u_lightBox) so the tab's highlight is swept across the panel's box. Measured at 3x, Home active (flush): top highlight 71/71 and 55/55 dark, 237/236 light across the join; body 44/44 and 213/213. 2026-11-17 second follow-up (owner: the corners read as a different texture, two surfaces made the tab): the glass now draws the whole selection. The shader takes u_fillet and draws the joined tab's concave corners itself, with the lit edge wrapping each curve and fading into the panel's unbeveled side. While the tab is live its box grows by --junction-corner above (unless flush) and below, the CSS .rail-junction-corner spans are hidden, and the tab paints its own show-through (--lg-backdrop: none), so no page surface sits under it. Measured at 3x with Index active: tab body vs panel body 43/44 dark and 212/212 light; both curves clean in both themes (evidence/design-overhaul/rail-tab-glass-corners-2026-11-17.png). With the panel collapsed the tab joins the sheet and stays CSS.

items.claim: Expressive restores gradient depth through the shared sheet ends (light lifts the top and keeps its foot; dark lifts the top a little and deepens the vignette); Calm stays flat; glass, rail tab and sheet stay continuous
items.note: styles.css --sheet-top (palette --sheet-from unless Expressive lifts it: +22% white light, +5% white dark) and Expressive dark --sheet-shade --sheet-to +34% black (was 22%); custom palettes excluded. The curve and its stops are unchanged, so liquid-glass reads --sheet-top/--sheet-shade (use-liquid-glass.ts, which now also re-reads on data-appearance-preset). At 1280x860, x=1000: light 206->187 by y=600 before, 217->190 after; dark 37->26 before, 47->28 after with a deeper foot. Before/after rendered with the old ends injected; Calm captures included in the evidence set (shell-calm-*).

items.claim: Under glass, every menu that opens off the composer (the + menu and its Connectors and Skills submenus, the model picker with its effort footer, Choose tools, and the / tool picker) is a pane of the composer's glass drawn by the liquid-glass renderer, with the conversation showing through its thinned body as it does through the composer's
items.note: 2026-11-17 owner ask. glass/menu-glass.tsx (useMenuGlass('composer'), or MenuGlass around the + menu: useLiquidGlass on a callback ref, since the popups mount only while open, keyed to the composer's material) is applied in composer-plus.tsx, model-picker.tsx (coss ComboboxPopup gains surfaceRef for its painting span), composer-connections.tsx and composer-tools.tsx (the vendored trigger popover gains surfaceRef, composed with its placement ref). styles.css: .glass-menu takes the composer-glass tokens; live, the popup's fill, hairline and inner highlight give way to the pane; .composer-menu's opaque fill applies only off glass. appearance.css: the opaque popover paint and the popover material rules skip .glass-menu and its contents. With the composer on paper nothing changes. Measured in populated-shell at 2x, Expressive Stone, both themes: each popup data-liquid=live with its canvas, background transparent, backdrop blur(6px). Evidence: evidence/design-overhaul/composer-menus-glass-2026-11-17.png. Seen while checking, not from this change: Theo's face perches over the / picker's last row (it does so with the glass classes removed too).
